style.description: One of: reasons | mistakes | questions | myths | tested. The run tells you which one to write in its hard constraints; echo that exact value here. The style fixes the headline formula and what each numbered item is.

look.description: OPTIONAL, and set by the renderer rather than written here: one of editorial | cards | pillars | scorecard | lander. It picks which template lays the page out and changes nothing about the copy, so leave it out -- the run resolves it from the style.

headline.description: 8-14 words, following THIS page's style formula exactly (the hard constraints quote it): reasons -> 'N Reasons <audience> Are Choosing <category>'; mistakes -> 'N Mistakes <audience> Make When Buying <category>'; questions -> 'N Questions <audience> Should Ask Before Buying <category>'; myths -> 'N <category> Myths <audience> Still Hear, and What the Evidence Says'; tested -> 'We Checked N <category> Claims <audience> Keep Hearing. Here Is What Held Up'. N is the number of entries in reasons in every style. Never contains a price. <audience> names the people the ad speaks to by their situation or goal (2-5 words), never a bare 'people' or 'buyers', never the company by name; <category> is the product category, never the company or a model name.

dek.description: One-line subhead under the headline, one sentence.

hero.description: The header's hero image slot -- one asset_id from facts_pack.assets, a lifestyle or installation photo in preference to a product-on-white shot.

reasons.description: 5-7 numbered items, in order (the field is named 'reasons', not 'items' -- 'items' collides with Python dict's own .items method under Jinja's attribute-then-subscript lookup; it holds this style's items whatever the style calls them). Each entry: number, an H2 heading, a 50-150 word body, one image, and a closing proof line.

heading.description: H2 heading for this item, <=10 words, no numeral (the renderer draws the number) and no price. What it asserts follows the page's style: a reason, a mistake, a question, a myth, or what held up under test.

claim_ids.description: The BODY's own citations: every claim_id behind a number, price, spec or trigger word in text. The proof line's claim_ids cover the proof line only -- when the body states the same fact, cite it here too.

proof.description: The item's closing proof line -- one short sentence that either cites a verified claim_id or is an attributed customer statement (attributed_to_customer: true, phrased as the customer's own words). An item with neither fails the gate.

audience_fit.description: The honest fit block: who this is for, and who it is not for. Two short lists of 2-4 one-line entries each. The 'not for you' list is the point -- name real, checkable limits (space, power, household size, budget), never a fake drawback or a humblebrag. Both lists are claims-safe: a line stating a number or a spec carries claim_ids.

faq.description: 5-7 questions a buyer actually asks before this purchase. Every answer that states a fact (a number, a price, a spec, or one of the trigger words) carries claim_ids.

answer.description: 2-4 sentences. Answer the question first, then the detail.

cta_text.description: The ONE CTA button text for this page, from allowed_cta_texts. The renderer reuses it verbatim in the header, after items 2 and 4, in the closing block, and in the sticky bottom bar -- choose it once here, never vary it.

cta_url.description: The CTA's destination URL, reused everywhere cta_text is. The one and only cta_url on the page.

closing.description: Closing block: a 3-bullet recap, the CTA, the fixed warranty sentence, and the allowed financing sentence given in the prompt's Financing rule.

headline.description: Optional short closing-band headline above the recap, e.g. 'Ready to feel the difference?'. Never contains a price.

recap.description: Exactly 3 bullets, each one line, recapping the page's three strongest points. A bullet stating a fact carries claim_ids.

warranty_line.description: Must be exactly the fixed warranty sentence -- see the global voice block.

financing_line.description: text: must be exactly the allowed financing sentence given in the prompt's Financing rule, verbatim -- see the global voice block. Never a freeform monthly figure, APR, or lender name typed in directly here.
